trust_decision.summary: instantiate() must never resolve, invoke, return or defer a config-selected callable that the active target policy denies; the decision is made on every name and every resolved/returned callable inside hydra/_internal/instantiate/_instantiate2.py, on both the legacy blocklist path and the explicit _target_whitelist_ path.

landing_point.why: The summary says the target blacklist is bypassed, so an engineer first reads the blocklist set and the matcher that decides whether a target is blocked (DEFAULT_BLOCKLISTED_MODULES at :21-90, _is_blocklisted_target at :150-155) and adds names there.

fix_sites.module_kind: internal policy data (blocklist sets and prefixes)
internal policy predicate over target names
internal call handler (invocation and returned-callable mediation)
internal identity resolver (security name of a resolved callable)
internal authorization and target resolution (both policy modes)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The dotpath primitives and helpers (_locate at hydra/_internal/utils.py:628, get_object/get_method/get_class at hydra/utils.py:27-90) are documented as trusted-code lookup APIs, not instantiate paths; the blocklist is an instantiate stopgap, so a solver can argue a Python caller passing a config string to get_object() is outside the advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An exact (non-wildcard) _target_whitelist_ entry for a re-exported target must keep working: json.JSONDecoder lives in json.decoder, so a fix that always rechecks the resolved identity rejects a deliberately authorized target and breaks tests/instantiate/test_instantiate.py:3778.

O6_input_shapes: plain dotpath string whose prefix is blocklisted directly (os.kill, posix.kill)
module-attribute alias string whose prefix looks benign (logging.os.system, multiprocessing.sharedctypes.ctypes.cdll.LoadLibrary)
accessor-suffixed spellings of the same object (os.system.__call__, builtins.type.__new__.__call__, operator.attrgetter.__new__)
already-resolved Python callable objects and bound descriptors passed as _target_ (os.system.__call__, classmethod(getattr).__get__, types.FunctionType)
config-supplied dotpath argument consumed by a discovery helper (_target_: hydra.utils.get_object / hydra._internal.utils._locate / builtins.getattr with path or _args_)
callable produced as a target's return value (getattr, functools.partial, discovery helpers)
deferred form: _partial_: true or functools.partial whose effective callable or keyword arguments are supplied at invocation time
nested containers: _args_ / kwargs / call-site override dicts holding further _target_ entries

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A target that returns a config-named callable but is not builtins.getattr, functools.partial or a discovery helper (e.g. builtins.dict.get over the dict from builtins.vars) is never blocklist-checked on the main-branch fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: dict.get/vars are ordinary data operations, not the 'producers' the report names; the main-branch fix mediates only the three listed producers, so the rest of the returned-callable family looks like a neighbouring feature.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function (_call_target), one line from the sink

O8_uncovered_routes.route: builtins.object.__getattribute__ / builtins.type.__getattribute__ as _target_ return a config-named attribute (including a blocklisted callable); they are absent from the legacy blocklist and are only refused when an explicit whitelist is active.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Attribute access is a legacy-compatible operation kept available on the legacy path in the published fix itself; a solver reads that as permission to leave it open.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same module, policy data versus call handler

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A fourth discovery helper next to get_class/get_method/get_object that also calls _locate.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Three near-identical helpers already sit in a row; a maintainer adding one more would document it but easily forget the internal DISCOVERY_TARGETS name set.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another alias of an existing discovery helper whose resolved identity differs from its documented name (get_static_method is already such an alias).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already aliases get_static_method = get_method, and the published fix lists the alias explicitly only because of that.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third policy mode or a new knob reusing _is_target_whitelisted/_authorize_target_name but with its own blocklist predicate.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The module already carries two parallel predicates (legacy blocklist and whitelist) and the fix has to keep three near-copies of the blocklist test in sync.

O9_family: incomplete denylist (CWE-184) leading to code execution through config-selected callables
